information_rule: Each candidate is ranked from the mover rack and public information only: every possible last tile is enumerated from the public unseen pool (distribution minus board minus own rack) and weighted by multiplicity; per-world reply features are aggregated before the single forward pass; the actual last tile is consumed only when the chosen move is played. Every fresh decision re-ran the policy with the actual last tile swapped for an opponent-rack tile and required bitwise-identical inputs and the same choice.

training_data.labels: depth2 endgame search per candidate per public hypothetical last tile (previous study); per-tile margin and W/T/L with multiplicity retained in scenarios.csv

features.v1: opp greedy reply, mover greedy follow-up, full greedy playout (BEST_SMALL) per world
features.v2: opp best-scoring reply via exact lane-incremental WMP search (+2x mover rack if out), out flag, tiles, pass flag; mover BEST_SMALL greedy follow-up (score+2x opp rack if out), out flag; aggregated mean/std/min/max over worlds; plus one-ply value (after - mean opp value); 68 public candidate scalars (value-net scalars minus 4 history entries), static equity, spread after

model: MLP 1x128 ReLU -> scalar; within-root loss: root-demeaned Huber(margin/10) + listwise softmax CE (T=4); AdamW 1e-3, wd 1e-3, 25 epochs, batch 32 roots; seed 20261014
selection_on_stored_data: 4-fold grouped CV over all 2816 stored roots (whole roots per fold) plus out-of-fold completed games; old 512 test roots used diagnostically only

labeled.labels: peg1data depth2, same procedure, PGO build

full_games.note: seat-swapped pair per game id; static play outside the 1PEG; continuation static (0) or fixed two-ply endgame (2)

fresh_sets.overlap: no fresh board equals any stored (2816) or prior (896) 1PEG board; all fresh boards distinct

evaluation.paired: per root: policy choice vs static top-1, same actual last tile, common continuation; pair win score (W_p+1-W_s)/2, pair spread (M_p-M_s)/2; 10,000 bootstrap resamples of roots
evaluation.timing: single process, warm page cache, policy PGO build, 512 fresh roots, no other compute jobs

exact_continuation.description: After the 1PEG pick is played with the actual last tile, one endgame_solve from the post-move position: 25 plies, 1 thread, no soft or hard time limit, one transposition table per process (fraction 0.03 of RAM for fresh set 2, 0.02 for the PEG and labelled runs) reused across solves, no two-ply TT. Mover final spread = (mover - opponent) - value if the opponent is on turn, + value if the mover is. proven = endgame_ctx_get_progress depth < 25; all solves are proven except 3 depth-limited picks (see depth_limited).
exact_continuation.pass_handling: A pass leaves the tile in the bag; the player then on turn plays MAGPIE's default PEG pick (peg_args_fill defaults: built-in stage schedule, nested lookahead caps 8/4/2, 1 thread, no time budget) until the bag is empty, then the exact solve.
exact_continuation.earlier_continuations_after_pass: Greedy-seed scoring (vnt_peg1_finish): after a pass the opponent played static top-1 at its own 1PEG; the two-ply variant resumed once the bag was empty. peg1play/peg1games: candidates were placements only and no forced pass occurred, so they never continued after a pass.
exact_continuation.pick_codes: >=0 static rank in the top-64 pool; -1 greedy seed over all moves (recomputed, must match the earlier run); -2 MAGPIE default PEG pick; -3 default PEG pick plus information-rule check
exact_continuation.peg_information_rule_check: default PEG pick rerun with the actual last tile swapped for an opponent-rack tile; fatal unless the pick is identical; 4/4 boards passed

board_order.note: seeded permutation; any complete prefix is an unbiased subset

fresh2.choosers: static, fast, fastU, fastUm, cascade, cascadeU, cascadeUm, strong, strongU, strongUm, greedy top64, greedy all; picks deduplicated per board
fresh2.stopped: 547-board prefix complete (1,745 picks); later chunks not run

pegfull.note: first 256 boards of the same fresh-set-2 order; static and default PEG pick

labeled.choosers: static, fast, strong, cascade, depth2 teacher margin-first and win-first

depth_limited.method: lldb read of worker 0 best_pv_value / completed_depth (scripts/eg_best.py, offsets scripts/eg_offsets.c). final = mover margin after the pick (-initial_spread) - best_pv_value. Rows with proven=1 in chunk-0034h/0041h were finished picks read from the processes' unflushed stdio buffers (scripts/eg_rows.py).
depth_limited.decision: User chose (2026-10-15) not to wait for a 24 h per-solve cutoff; the deepest completed iterative-deepening value is used and the row is marked proven=0.
depth_limited.scripts: exact/fresh2/DEPTH_LIMITED.json; scripts/eg_offsets.c (struct offsets), eg_peek.py (live progress), eg_best.py (completed-depth value), eg_rows.py (unflushed rows)

exact_continuation.buffered_rows: peg1exact flushes a board's rows only when all its picks finish. Finished picks of boards 2562 and 4328 were read from the processes' stdio buffers (chunk-0034h, chunk-0041h); the remaining picks of chunks 34 and 41 ran as side chunks (chunk-0034s2-s5, chunk-0041s2-s3). The analyzer keys rows by (root, code), so all files merge. Side runs reproduced 4328 picks 1 and 6 exactly.
exact_continuation.run_conditions: Solve and PEG timings were taken on a shared, oversubscribed machine (up to 14 CPU-bound processes on 10 cores) and are indicative only.
